content.value_statement: Deep learning repositories can be hard to understand before making changes. This skill maps structure, entrypoints, configs, evaluation contracts, and suspicious patterns without modifying code.
actual_capabilities: Identify likely training, inference, evaluation, model, and config entrypoints.
Create summary, risk, research map, change map, eval contract, and status outputs.
Inspect Python and config-like files with lightweight static heuristics.
Highlight conservative insertion points and protected evaluation zones.
Accept optional JSON or YAML context for dataset, benchmark, task, and metric hints.
limitations: Does not prove bugs or benchmark claims.
Does not run training or heavy evaluation jobs by default.
Can miss logic hidden in unsupported file types or generated code.
Parent-directory references should be reviewed before restricted marketplace use.

use_cases.title: Research Onboarding
use_cases.description: Map a new model repository before changing architecture, configs, or evaluation scripts.

use_cases.title: Change Planning
use_cases.description: Find likely insertion points and protected evaluation areas before assigning implementation work.

use_cases.title: Review Preparation
use_cases.description: Create a structured project summary and risk list before a code review or reproduction attempt.

prompt_templates.title: Map The Repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this deep learning repository. Summarize the model structure, training entrypoints, inference entrypoints, evaluation entrypoints, and key configs.

prompt_templates.title: Find Insertion Points
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this project for safe insertion points for a new module. Separate likely edit zones from protected evaluation and data handling zones.

prompt_templates.title: Define Evaluation Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository and define the evaluation contract. Include dataset, benchmark, metric, metric direction, command source, and expected artifacts.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Research Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a conservative read-only audit of this repository. Flag suspicious implementation patterns as heuristics and explain what evidence is still needed.

output_examples.input: Analyze a vision transformer project before I add a new prediction head.
output: A project summary identifies model, train, inference, and evaluation entrypoints.
A change map separates likely head insertion files from protected metric and dataset code.
A risk note lists suspicious patterns that need manual confirmation.

output_examples.input: Create an evaluation contract for a segmentation repository.
output: The report names the task family, dataset, benchmark, primary metric, and metric direction.
It records the likely evaluation command source and expected result artifacts.
It highlights missing context that must be resolved before comparison.

output_examples.input: Review a new research repository without changing files.
output: The analysis lists key files and relationships in plain language.
It provides conservative suggestions for next reading steps.
It avoids claiming unverified heuristics as confirmed bugs.

best_practices: Run it before editing model, training, or evaluation code.
Provide task, dataset, benchmark, and metric context when available.
Treat suspicious pattern output as review guidance, not proof.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to run training jobs, downloads, or environment setup.
Treating heuristic risk notes as confirmed defects without evidence.
Using it as a replacement for benchmark reproduction or security review.

faq.question: Does this skill modify repository code?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for read-only analysis and structured reporting.

faq.question: Can it run training or evaluation commands?
faq.answer: No. It should avoid heavy execution and focus on static project understanding.

faq.question: What kinds of repositories fit best?
faq.answer: It fits deep learning and machine learning research repositories with Python, configs, and evaluation scripts.

faq.question: What outputs should I expect?
faq.answer: It can produce a summary, risk notes, research map, change map, evaluation contract, and status report.

faq.question: Does it prove that a suspicious pattern is a bug?
faq.answer: No. It labels suspicious patterns as heuristics until command-level or test evidence confirms them.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
